::: {#thm-euler-trail}
#### Euler trails and odd degrees

Let $G$ be a connected graph (@def-connected), and let $u$ and $v$ be different vertices of $G$.
Then $G$ has an Euler trail (@def-euler-trail) from $u$ to $v$ if and only if
$u$ and $v$ have odd degree (@def-degree) and every other vertex has even degree.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Let $G'$ be the graph $G$ with one new edge $h$ with endpoints $u$ and $v$.
It may be parallel (@def-parallel-edges) to an edge of $G$.
$G'$ is connected, and has at least one edge.
The edge $h$ adds 1 to the degrees of $u$ and $v$, and changes no other degree.
So the condition on the degrees in $G$ says exactly that every vertex has even degree in $G'$.

**Only if.**
Let $u = v_0, e_1, \ldots, e_n, v_n = v$ be an Euler trail of $G$.
Adding $h$ at the end gives the circuit $v_0, e_1, \ldots, e_n, v, h, u$ in $G'$,
which contains every edge of $G'$.
So every vertex has even degree in $G'$, by @thm-euler-circuit.

**If.**
Every vertex has even degree in $G'$,
so $G'$ has an Euler circuit, by @thm-euler-circuit, and $h$ is one of its edges.
A circuit can start at any of its vertices:
moving the part before a vertex to the end gives a circuit with the same edges.
Reading a circuit backward gives a circuit with the same edges,
so we may assume that the Euler circuit crosses $h$ from $v$ to $u$.
So $G'$ has an Euler circuit that starts at $v$ with the edge $h$, as $v, h, u, \ldots, v$.
Leaving out $v$ and $h$ at the start gives a trail from $u$ to $v$ that contains every edge of $G$.

:::

:::
